p1.examiner: Look at the two pictures. Here the guitar is next to the bed, but here it is on the bed. What other differences can you see?
differences: In your picture there are two footballs, but in my picture there is one.
In your picture the camera is on the desk, but in my picture it is on the chair.
In your picture the boy is reading a comic, but in my picture he is sleeping.
In your picture the bike is green, but in my picture it is red.
In your picture there is a photo on the wall, but in my picture there is a clock.

p2.title: Lucy's football game
p2.examiner_open: These pictures show a story. It's called 'Lucy's football game'. Look at the pictures first. Lucy wants to play football with the boys, but they say no. Now you tell the story.
frames: Lucy wants to play football with the boys in the park, but they say no because she is a girl.
Lucy practises next to the wall every afternoon. She kicks the ball again and again.
One day, a boy is ill and the group needs one more player. They ask Lucy to play with them.
Lucy plays very well and she gets two goals. Now she plays with the group every Saturday.

p1: Part One. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Grandma, this is the park where we go on Saturdays.
It's beautiful. Who's the girl on the bike?
That's Daisy. Her bike has got a red bag for her books.
Can you see the line? This is an example. Now you listen and draw lines.
And who's the boy under the tree with the guitar?
That's Ben. He plays the guitar in the park because his house is very small.
Who's the girl with the paints?
That's Alice. She's painting the lake with the ducks. She paints every Saturday.
Can you see the boy with the camera?
Yes! Is he taking a photo of the ducks?
Yes, that's Sam. He takes photos of animals and birds.
And the girl on the grass? She's reading.
That's Lucy. She's reading a comic. She's got hundreds of them at home.
And that boy is playing football with two friends.
Paul. He wants to be a football player.
Now listen to Part One again.
p2: Part Two. Listen and look. There is one example.
Mum, there are music lessons at school!
That's good news. Which day are they? Wednesday?
Can you see the answer? Now you listen and write.
Which teacher is going to help you?
Mr Baker. B-A-K-E-R. He plays six instruments!
At five, after our last lesson.
Five o'clock. I can come for you at six, then.
Sixteen. Ten girls and six boys.
Are you going to learn the guitar?
No, I've got a guitar at home. I want to learn the piano.
The piano! Your grandfather played the piano.
Where are they? In the classroom?
No, in the library. It's the biggest room and there's a piano there.
Now listen to Part Two again.
p3: Part Three. Listen and look. There is one example.
Alice is telling her grandmother what her family does at the weekend. What does each person do?
Alice, what do you do at the weekend?
I dance! I go to a dance class on Saturday morning with my friend.
Can you see the letter F? Now you listen and write a letter in each box.
She plays tennis. She's very good and she plays with the woman next door.
He takes photos. Photos of buildings, of the river, of us... He's got three cameras!
And your brother? Does he play tennis too?
No, he swims. He goes to the swimming pool every Sunday morning.
Does your grandfather come with you?
No, he stays at home and plays the piano. He plays old songs and we all sing.
My cousin rides a horse. She lives in the countryside and she's got two horses.
Now listen to Part Three again.
p4: Part Four. Look at the pictures. Listen and look. There is one example.
Sam, do you paint like your sister?
No, I take photos. I've got my father's old camera.
I listen to music, but I can't play anything.
Can you see the tick? Now you listen and tick the box.
One. What did Lucy get for her birthday?
Did you get a new bike for your birthday, Lucy?
No, I got a guitar! My brother got the bike last year.
Two. Where do the children play tennis?
Do you play tennis in the park?
We can't. We play at school, after our lessons.
Three. When does Ben practise the piano?
Ben, do you practise before school?
No, I get up too late. I practise in the evening, after dinner.
Four. What are Paul and his friends going to do?
We're going to the park on Saturday. My mother is making sandwiches for all of us.
A picnic! Are you going to swim too?
No, the water is very cold now.
Five. Which film did Zoe like best?
Zoe, did you like the film about the animals?
It was good, but my favourite was the film about the sea. There were beautiful fish in it.
And the film about the plane?
Now listen to Part Four again.
p5: Part Five. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
Here's a picture of a bedroom. Can you see the guitar next to the bed?
Can you see the brown guitar? This is an example. Now you listen and colour and write.
Now, can you see the football under the desk?
There's a camera on the desk. Can I colour it?
A red camera. That's a funny colour for a camera!
Can you see the comic on the floor?
Yes. There's a board on the wall with nothing on it. Write the word 'music'. M-U-S-I-C.
And now the bike behind the door. Colour it green, please.
Well done. That's a very busy bedroom!
Now listen to Part Five again.
